chapter: Own bands and Los Angeles clubs
title: Playing the Alabam five times and demanding pay before going on
summary: Curtis Mosby's Alabam had changing owners; Lee would not go on the bandstand until the box office paid him each night.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So that's the place that I can't put any -- when it was on it, because I worked at the Club Alabam about 3 or 4 different times -- maybe 5 times, I don't know.
This is the first time you've mentioned anything, but when you were 13.
Yeah, but no, no. I worked there afterwards because ...
That was the Apex.
Yeah, the Apex. But I think I did say that -- did I tell you that Curtis Mosby owned the Apex, right? But then in later years, somehow he got involved in the Alabam again, and he got it back.
So he didn't have it for awhile, is that right?
Oh, for a long time, he didn't have it.
Because I was told that it was owned by some Italian brothers.
Yeah, it sure was.
Was that in between?
That was in between, yeah. I'm sure of that.
In between Curtis Mosby's ownerships?

Right. So I don't know the way I was running around, because I was a maverick; I would play every place, you know -- any place. So that's why it is hard for me to tell you when I was at the Alabam, but I must have worked at the Alabam 5 different times. I worked there with Baron Morehead's band, I worked there with Lorenzo Flanoy's band -- he was there at one time when he had Dootsie Williams in the band; and Joe Lewis was playing guitar. Those are some of the guys I can remember.

Then I played there when Curtis Mosby had the band because at the time, they were in kind of bad shape, and they wanted me to play, and I understood the musicians were not getting paid regularly, right? And so I made my deal that I would play, but the girl at the boxoffice had to pay me every night before I played, you know, so I made my own deals.
And I wouldn't go on until I got my money; I wouldn't go on the bandstand. I got paid every night because I thought it was just horrible for someone to work and not be paid, you know.
You're right.
And so -- a lot of the musicians used to get stiffed, a lot of times, waiting for the end of the

week -- and so when they had that type of reputation, I would say, 'Yeah, I'll work, but I have to paid in advance every night.' And so I would be sitting on the side and wait for them to bring me my money and then I would go get on the bandstand and play.
But I played there at least 5 times.
Did your first wife, Louise, Little Bow, she was called, ever work at the Alabam?
Oh yeah, sure she did.
I thought she did.
Yes, certainly she did. Yeah, she worked there.
And then she was also in 'Jump for Joy' wasn't she?
